title: APERTURE Commercial 4D — research evidence register
disclaimer: Research-derived design hypotheses; do not treat benchmark results as verified commercial performance. No live company data is included.

studies.title: Can LLMs Be CEOs? Benchmarking Strategic Resource Reallocation with Multi-Role Agent Simulation
studies.finding: Competing CFO, CTO, COO and CMO advice in multi-round resource allocation exposes strategic calibration failures despite structurally valid plans.
studies.aperture: Compare business-unit allocations while retaining conflicting assumptions and history; require human executive approval.

studies.title: Agentic ERP: Multi-Agent Large Language Model Architecture for Autonomous Enterprise Resource Planning
studies.finding: A graph-orchestrated role-aligned approach with risk-tiered human oversight was evaluated against ERP operations baselines, including a simulated operating year.
studies.aperture: Maintain typed enterprise state and explicit owner, action and approval edges; do not imply production integrations.

studies.title: TodoEvolve: Learning to Architect Agent Planning Systems
studies.finding: Task-specific planning structures can be revised dynamically rather than fixed to one hand-crafted process.
studies.aperture: Choose a constraint-appropriate planning strategy per engagement rather than a single universal agent chain.

studies.title: CoPE: A Framework for Optimizing Coordination between Planning and Execution in LLM-based Agents
studies.finding: Plan-deviated trajectories can undermine long-horizon outcomes; the paper studies tighter plan-execution coordination.
studies.aperture: Record expected and observed states, compare deviations, and re-plan only on validated triggers.

studies.title: Plan-and-Patch: Diffusion Language Models for Agentic Planning
studies.finding: Repairing affected plan regions while preserving unaffected steps can improve re-planning; results are benchmark- and model-specific.
studies.aperture: Patch the affected tasks and preserve approved commitments when new constraints invalidate part of a plan.

studies.title: EAIR: Interaction Risks in Enterprise LLM Multi-Agent Systems
studies.finding: Individually permitted agent actions can collectively violate enterprise constraints; executable micro-worlds support diagnosis and retest.
studies.aperture: Enforce shared company-level caps for cash, capacity, authority and commitments across business lines.

studies.title: Responsibility Boundaries for Agentic Systems: A Comparative Evaluation of Probabilistic Agentic Programming
studies.finding: An explicit mediation kernel can bind actions to authority, limits, approval and evidence under stated assumptions.
studies.aperture: Keep proposals separate from external execution and require action-specific approval and a logged decision.

studies.title: FACTS-MAS: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Adaptive Forecasting from Heterogeneous Evidence
studies.finding: Forecast evidence channels should be backtested and selectively weighted; a simpler exponential-smoothing method can remain competitive.
studies.aperture: Always benchmark against a simple baseline and track evidence usefulness before adding specialist models.

studies.title: Benchmarking Forecasting Agents on Yesterday's Tomorrows
studies.finding: Historical event archives can assess forecasts without using information unavailable at prediction time.
studies.aperture: Use as-of data snapshots, prospective forecasts, and leakage-safe historical comparisons.

studies.title: Towards Elastic Least Privilege for Agent Planning
studies.finding: Proposes limited, time-bound authority leases and planner-visible costs; operational effectiveness remains an open question.
studies.aperture: Give each commercial agent the least access required; escalate through user approval instead of broad privileges.
